title: The Story of the Porter and the Three Ladies

paragraphs.en: I heard that once in Baghdad, there lived a bachelor porter. One day, while he was standing in the market with his basket, a woman approached him. She wore a Mosul cloak, a silk veil, and a gold-embroidered kerchief tied with fluttering laces.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说在巴格达曾有一位单身搬运工。有一天，他在市场上抱着篮子站着时，一个女人走近了他。她穿着摩苏尔的长袍，戴着丝绸面纱，头巾上绣着金色花纹，并用飘动的丝带系着。

paragraphs.en: When she lifted her veil, her dark eyes with long lashes shone brightly. With a soft voice, she said, "Porter, take your basket and follow me." The porter, hardly believing his ears, took the basket and hurried behind her, exclaiming, "O lucky day, O happy day."
paragraphs.zh: 当她掀起面纱，一双长睫毛衬托下的黑眸闪烁着光芒。她用温柔的声音说道：“搬运工，请拿着篮子跟我走。”搬运工几乎不敢相信自己的耳朵，接过篮子匆匆跟在她身后，脱口而出：“多么幸运的一天！多么快乐的一天！”

paragraphs.en: She led him to a house where an old Christian answered the door. She gave him a dinar and received an olive green jug of wine in return. Placing the jug in the porter's basket, she said, "Porter, take your basket and follow me."
paragraphs.zh: 她领着他来到一所房子，门被一位年迈的基督徒打开。她给了他一枚第纳尔，换回了一只深绿色的酒壶。将酒壶放入搬运工的篮子后，她说：“搬运工，拿着你的篮子跟我来。”

paragraphs.en: The porter agreed, saying, "Very well, O auspicious day, O lucky day, O happy day," as he lifted the basket and followed her.
paragraphs.zh: 搬运工应允了，嘴里念叨着：“好日子啊，吉祥的日子啊，幸福的日子啊”，一边提起篮子跟着她走了。

paragraphs.en: She led him to a fruit vendor where she bought yellow and red apples, Hebron peaches, Turkish quinces, seacoast lemons, royal oranges, and baby cucumbers. She also purchased Aleppo jasmine, Damascus lilies, myrtle berries, mignonettes, daisies, gillyflowers, lilies of the valley, irises, narcissus, daffodils, violets, anemones, and pomegranate blossoms. She placed all these items in the porter's basket and asked him to follow her.
paragraphs.zh: 她领着他来到一个水果摊，买了黄澄澄和红彤彤的苹果、希伯仑桃子、土耳其榅桲、海滨柠檬、皇室橘子以及小黄瓜。她还买了一些大马士革茉莉花、迷迭香百合、冬青果、小雏菊、康乃馨、水仙、风信子、紫罗兰、风信子和石榴花。她把这些东西都装进了搬运工的篮子里，然后让他跟着她走。

paragraphs.en: She went to the butcher's, bought fresh mutton, and asked the porter to follow her. At the grocer’s, she purchased various condiments including olives, tarragon, and cheese. She then headed to the dry goods store where she bought raisins, sugar canes, figs, chick-peas, pistachios, almonds, and hazelnuts.
paragraphs.zh: 她先去了肉铺，买了一块新鲜的羊肉，然后请搬运工跟着她。接着在杂货店买了各种调料，包括橄榄、塔尔草和奶酪。随后，她前往干货店，购买了葡萄干、糖 cane 、无花果、鹰嘴豆、 Pistachio、杏仁和榛子。

paragraphs.en: The porter carried the basket as they moved on to the confectioner’s shop, where she filled a tray with pastries and sweets like rolls and cookies. Afterward, at the druggist's, she bought scented waters, musk, aloewood, and other items before adding two loaves of sugar and candles.
paragraphs.zh: 搬运工提着篮子，随着她们来到糖果店，那里摆放了一盘各式糕点和甜食，如小面包和饼干。接着，在药剂师那儿，她购买了香水中草、麝香、安息香以及其他物品，并添上了两块糖面包和蜡烛。

paragraphs.en: She placed everything in the basket and instructed the porter to follow her. They arrived at a large courtyard outside a grand mansion with massive pillars and an ivory- and gold-inlaid door. She knocked gently on the door.
paragraphs.zh: 她把所有东西都放在篮子里，吩咐搬运工跟在后面。他们来到了一座宏伟宅邸外面的一个宽敞庭院，那里有巨大的柱子和镶嵌着象牙与金饰的大门。她轻轻地敲了敲门。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad asked Shahrazad, "Sister, if you're not sleepy, tell us a story." Shahrazad replied, "I hear and obey."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，丁拉兹问道：“姐姐，如果你不困的话，给我们讲个故事吧。”沙赫札德回答说：“我听你的，遵命。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad began: As the porter stood with his basket at the door behind the girl, marveling at her beauty and grace, the door opened. A full-figured young woman, about five feet tall, entered. She was charming, graceful, and elegant.
paragraphs.zh: 沙海拉扎德说道：当搬运工站在门口后面，女孩的身后，惊叹于她的美丽与优雅时，门开了。进来的是一个身材丰满、身高约五英尺左右的年轻人。她魅力十足，举止优雅，气质高雅。

paragraphs.en: Her forehead resembled a new moon, eyes like those of a deer or wild heifer, eyebrows like the crescent in Sha’ban, cheeks like red anemones, mouth like Solomon's seal, lips like carnelian, teeth like pearls set in coral, neck like a king’s cake, bosom like a fountain, breasts like big pomegranates, and belly with a navel like a cup holding benzoin ointment. The poet aptly described her as:
paragraphs.zh: 她的前额宛如新月，眼睛像鹿或野牛般灵动，眉毛如同沙班月牙，脸颊犹如鲜红的海葵，嘴唇似红玉，牙齿如珍珠嵌在珊瑚中，颈项宛若王饼，胸部如泉涌般丰盈，乳房大得像石榴，腹部中央则像盛着安息香膏的小杯。诗人恰到好处地形容她为：

paragraphs.en: On stately sun and full moon cast your sight; Savor the flowers and lavender's delight.
paragraphs.zh: 在庄严的日光和圆满的月色中凝望；品味那些花朵与薰衣草带来的愉悦。

paragraphs.en: Your eyes have never seen such white in black, Such radiant face with hair so deeply dark.
paragraphs.zh: 你从未见过如此黑白分明的纯净， 如此光彩照人的容颜与深邃的黑发。

paragraphs.en: With rosy cheeks, Beauty proclaimed her name, To those who had not yet received her fame.
paragraphs.zh: 面颊红润的美丽自报家门，向那些尚未闻其大名的人们宣告。

paragraphs.en: Her swaying hips brought joy, but her slender waist caused sorrow.
paragraphs.zh: 她的摇曳身姿令人愉悦，但那纤细的腰肢却让人感到一丝哀愁。

paragraphs.en: The porter was so struck by the girl that he nearly dropped his basket. "Never have I seen a better day!" he exclaimed.
paragraphs.zh: 搬运工被那女孩深深吸引，几乎连篮子都拿不住了。“这是我见过的最好的一天！”他脱口而出。

paragraphs.en: The doorkeeper directed the shopper to enter and help the porter. They went into a grand hall, where the doorkeeper followed them.
paragraphs.zh: 门房引导购物者进入，并协助搬运工。他们走进了一个宽敞的大厅，门房随后跟了进来。

paragraphs.en: The hall was spacious and splendid, with arched compartments and niches adorned with carved woodwork. A booth hung with drapes stood there, along with closets and cupboards covered in curtains. In the center of the hall was a large pool with a fountain, and at the far end lay a couch made of black juniper wood, draped in white silk and embellished with gems and pearls.
paragraphs.zh: 大厅宽敞而华丽，拱形的隔间和壁龛雕刻着精美的木饰。一排挂着帷幔的小摊位矗立其中，旁边是覆盖着窗帘的橱柜和壁橱。厅中央有一个大水池，池中有一座喷泉；而在厅的远端，则摆放着一张用黑樱桃木制成的长沙发，上面铺着洁白的丝绸，并镶嵌着宝石和珍珠。

paragraphs.en: A red silk canopy, fastened with large pearls, hung over it.
paragraphs.zh: 一顶红色丝质帷幔，用大颗珍珠固定着，悬挂在上方。

paragraphs.en: A radiant girl emerged from behind the curtain. She had an elegant figure, the scent of ambergris, sugared lips, Babylonian eyes, arched eyebrows like bent bows, and a face that outshone the sun. Her beauty was compared to a great star in the sky, a golden dome, or a unveiled bride.
paragraphs.zh: 一位光彩照人的少女从幕后走出。她身材优雅，身上弥漫着龙涎香的气息，嘴唇如蜜糖般甜美，眼睛深邃似古巴比伦的宝石，眉毛弯如弓箭，脸庞更是光芒万丈，胜过太阳。她的美丽被形容为夜空中的一颗巨星、金色的穹顶或是未揭面纱的新娘。

paragraphs.en: The third girl joined her sisters, urging them to help the porter. Together, they lifted his basket, emptied its contents, and arranged fruits, pickles, flowers, and herbs neatly. They then gave him one dinar.
paragraphs.zh: 第三个女孩加入姐妹们，催促她们帮助搬运工。大家合力抬起他的篮子，倒出里面的东西，将水果、腌菜、鲜花和草药整齐地摆放好。随后，她们给了他一枚第纳尔。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused as morning approached. Dinarzad remarked on the story's wonder, and Shahrazad promised a stranger tale if she lived to tell it again the next night.
paragraphs.zh: 随着晨光渐近，沙赫拉兹德停下了讲述。丁纳札德对这个故事感到惊奇不已，沙赫拉兹德承诺如果她能活到第二天晚上，还会带来一个更加离奇的故事。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad asked her sister Shahrazad to continue the story of the three girls. Shahrazad agreed with pleasure.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达请她的妹妹沙赫拉兹达继续讲述那三个女孩的故事。沙赫拉兹达欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: When the porter saw the beautiful girls and their abundant provisions for feasting, he was surprised by their solitude. One girl questioned him: "Why don't you leave? Do you think your pay is too little?"
paragraphs.zh: 当门夫看到这三个美貌女子及其丰盛的宴席准备，不禁对她们的孤身出行感到惊讶。其中一个女孩问道：“你怎么还不走？你觉得工资太少吗？”

paragraphs.en: She then turned to her sister and said, "Give him another dinar." The porter replied that his pay was sufficient but wondered about the girls' situation.
paragraphs.zh: 她随后转向妹妹说：“再给他一个第纳尔。”搬运工回答说，自己的报酬已经足够了，但还是对这三个女孩的情况感到好奇。

paragraphs.en: He suggested they needed a fourth person for complete pleasure, quoting a poet who wrote:
paragraphs.zh: 他建议她们还需要第四个人才能获得完整的快乐，并引用了一位诗人的诗句。

paragraphs.en: "For our delight four things we need, the lute, The harp, the zither, and the double flute, Blending with the scent of four lovely flowers, Roses, myrtles, anemones, and gillyflowers. Only in four such things join together, Money, and wine, and youth, and a lover."
paragraphs.zh: 为了让我们感到愉悦，我们需要四件事物：竖琴、古筝、琵琶和双管笛，它们与四种芬芳的花朵——玫瑰、冬青、风信子和番红花交织在一起。只有当金钱、美酒、青春和爱人齐聚一堂时，才能达到这样的完美境界。

paragraphs.en: The girls laughed. They argued that as women who kept their secrets, they couldn't entrust them to strangers, quoting ibn al-Tammam: "Your own secret to none reveal; It will be lost when it is told. If your own breast cannot conceal, How can another better hold?"
paragraphs.zh: 女孩们笑了。她们争辩说，作为保守秘密的女性，不能将秘密托付给陌生人，引述了伊本·图马曼的话：“自己的秘密勿轻言；言说之时已成空。若非自己胸中藏，他人安能替你守？”

paragraphs.en: Hearing this, the porter assured them he was a sensible and wise man who had studied sciences and learned well. He promised to keep their secrets safe, quoting another poet: "Only the faithful does a secret keep; None but the best can hold it unrevealed. I keep a secret in a well-shut house of which the key is lost and the lock sealed."
paragraphs.zh: 听到这话，守门人保证自己是个理智而明智的人，学识渊博且深谙各种学问。他承诺会为她们保守秘密，并引用另一位诗人的诗句：“唯有忠诚者能守护秘密；唯有最好的人才能将之严密封锁。我将秘密藏于一扇紧闭的房子里，钥匙遗失，门锁封死。”

paragraphs.en: The girls challenged the porter to pay for their entertainment. The mistress quoted a saying about love needing gain. The doorkeeper urged him to show he had something.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩们要求搬运工支付她们的娱乐费用。女主人引用了一句关于爱情需要付出的话。门房催促他拿出点实际行动来。

paragraphs.en: The shopper intervened, praising his service and offering to pay for him. Grateful, the porter thanked her and offered to return the dinar she gave him.
paragraphs.zh: 购物者插话说了几句感谢的话，并主动提出要付钱给他。porter感激地向她道谢，并表示愿意把那枚第纳尔还给她。

paragraphs.en: The shopper then prepared the banquet. She tidied up, strained wine, and arranged bowls, cups, and plates. Setting the table by a pool, she invited everyone to join.
paragraphs.zh: 购物者随后准备了盛宴。她整理好房间，过滤酒液，并摆放好了碗、杯和盘子。她在池塘边布置好餐桌，请大家一同享用。

paragraphs.en: Her sisters helped as the porter marveled at his good fortune.
paragraphs.zh: 她的姐妹们在一旁帮忙，而搬运工则惊叹于自己的好运气。

paragraphs.en: The shopper filled her first cup, drank it, and passed another to one of her sisters. Then she gave a third to the other sister and a fourth to the porter. He held it, bowed, thanked her, and recited:
paragraphs.zh: 购物者先给自己倒了一杯，喝完后又给其中一个妹妹递过去。接着她给另一个妹妹倒了一杯，再给搬运工倒了一杯。搬运工接过杯子，微微鞠了一躬，道了声谢，并朗诵了一句什么。

paragraphs.en: "Drink not the cup save with a friend you trust, One whose blood to noble forefathers owes. Wine, like the wind, is sweet if o'er the sweet, And foul if o'er the foul it haply blows."
paragraphs.zh: “除非你信任的朋友，出自高贵先祖的血脉，否则切勿独饮此杯。酒如风，甘甜之时令人陶醉，污浊之际则成毒药。”

paragraphs.en: He emptied his cup. The doorkeeper responded with:
paragraphs.zh: 他一饮而尽。门房回答道：

paragraphs.en: "Cheers, and drink it in good health; This wine is good for your health."
paragraphs.zh: 干杯，祝你健康；这酒对身体有益。

paragraphs.en: The porter thanked her and kissed her hand. After drinking again, he turned to his companion, the shopper, saying, "My lady, your servant is calling on you," and recited:
paragraphs.zh: 门夫感激地向她道谢并吻了她的手。喝完酒后，他转向同伴——那位购物者，说道：“夫人，您的仆人前来拜访您了。”然后吟诵起来：

paragraphs.en: One of your slaves waits at your door, With gratitude for your favor.
paragraphs.zh: 你的一个仆人守候在门外， 满怀感激之情。

paragraphs.en: She replied, "By God, welcome! Drink this wine; it relieves pain and restores health." The porter drank, then poured another cup.
paragraphs.zh: 她回答说：“上帝保佑，欢迎！喝这杯酒吧，它能缓解疼痛，恢复健康。” Porter喝了之后，又倒了一杯。

paragraphs.en: He kissed her hand, offered it to her, and recited:
paragraphs.zh: 他亲吻了她的手，将它递给她，并朗诵道：

paragraphs.en: I gave you pure old wine, red as cheeks, Which glowed like a furnace. You kissed the brim and smiled, asking, "How can cheeks repay what they owe?"
paragraphs.zh: 我给你的是纯正的老酒，红润如脸颊，犹如炉火般闪耀。你亲吻着杯沿微微一笑，问道：“脸颊又怎能偿还它们所欠的呢？”

paragraphs.en: I said, "Drink! This wine is my blood and tears, And my soul is in this cup."
paragraphs.zh: 我说：“喝吧！这酒是我的血和泪，我的灵魂就在这杯中。”

paragraphs.en: She replied, "If for me you shed your blood, I will gladly drink this red wine."
paragraphs.zh: 她回答说：“如果你为我流血，我愿意痛饮这杯红酒。”

paragraphs.en: The girls took turns serving him. One fed him a morsel, another flirted, and yet another offered fresh herbs or sweets until he was drunk. They danced and sang, with the porter toying, kissing, biting, and rubbing them.
paragraphs.zh: 姑娘们轮流伺候他。一个给他送食，另一个挑逗，还有个则送上新鲜的草药或甜点，直到把他灌醉。她们跳舞唱歌，搬运工则嬉戏、亲吻、咬弄和抚弄着她们。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, interrupting their revelry.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，打断了他们的狂欢。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused, then Dinarzad said, "What an amazing story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait for tomorrow's tale."
paragraphs.zh: 沙海拉扎德停顿了一下，然后迪纳兹达说道：“真是个令人惊叹的故事！”沙海拉扎德回答道：“请期待明天的故事吧。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad asked, "Sister, tell us a lovely little tale to pass the time." Shahrazad agreed with pleasure.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，丁纳兹德问道：“姐姐，请给我们讲一个可爱的小故事打发时间吧。”沙赫拉兹德欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: The doorkeeper entered the pool, splashed water over herself and her sisters, then sat naked in the porter's lap. Pointing to her slit, she asked, "My lord and my love, what is this?" The porter replied, "Your womb," but she slapped him, saying, "Pooh, pooh, you have no shame."
paragraphs.zh: 门房走进水池，溅了自己和姐妹们一身水，然后赤裸着身子坐在搬运工的膝上。她指着自己的私处问道：“我的老爷，我的爱人，这是什么？”搬运工回答说：“那是你的子宫。”但她一巴掌打在他脸上，嗔道：“哼，哼，你没羞耻心！”

paragraphs.en: He continued, "Your vulva," as one sister pinched him, shouting, "Bah, that's an ugly word." Then he said, "Your cunt," and another sister hit him on the chest, knocking him over. "Fie, have some shame," she exclaimed.
paragraphs.zh: 他继续说道：“你的私处。”这时，一位姐姐捏了他一下，喊道：“呸，这是个粗俗的词。”接着他又说：“你的阴道。”另一位姐姐则重重地打了他胸口一掌，把他打倒在地。“羞耻啊，你该有点廉耻心。”她大声说道。

paragraphs.en: He persisted with other names: "Your clitoris," "your pudenda, your pussy, your sex tool." Each time, one of the girls hit or slapped him, asking, "What do you call this?" Finally, the naked girl said, "The basil of the bridges."
paragraphs.zh: 他继续叫唤着其他名字：“你的阴蒂，”“你的外阴，你的私处，你的性器官。”每次说完，其中一个女孩都会打他一巴掌或给他一拳，并问道：“你这是指什么？”最后，那个赤裸的女孩说道：“这就是桥墩草。”

paragraphs.en: The porter cried out, "The basil of the bridges! You should have told me this from the beginning, oh, oh!" They then passed a cup and continued drinking.
paragraphs.zh: 门房喊道：“桥边的百里香！你应该一开始就告诉我，哦，哦！”他们随后递过一个杯子，继续喝了起来。

paragraphs.en: The shopper undressed, entered the pool, and washed herself thoroughly. She then rushed out, sat on the porter's lap, and asked, "My lord, what is this?" He replied, "Your vulva," to which she responded with a loud slap.
paragraphs.zh: 购物者脱去衣物，进入泳池，彻底清洗自己。随后她匆匆跑出泳池，坐到搬运工的膝上，问道：“大人，这是什么？”搬运工回答说：“你的私处。”她闻言当即给了他一个响亮的耳光。

paragraphs.en: He continued, "Your womb," prompting her sister to hit him. The third sister joined in, saying, "Fie, you are shameless." They kept hitting him until he cried out, "The basil of the bridges," causing them all to laugh.
paragraphs.zh: 他接着说道：“你们的子宫”，话音未落，他的姐姐便一巴掌打了过来。第三个姐姐也跟着附和道：“哎呀，你真是无耻。”她们继续打着他，直到他痛呼一声“桥边的百里香”，顿时大家都笑作一团。

paragraphs.en: However, they slapped him again and asked for the correct name.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，他们又给了他一巴掌，要求他报出正确的名字。

paragraphs.en: He suggested, "Why don’t you say 'the husked sesame'?" He was relieved when she agreed, saying, "The husked sesame!" They then dressed and sat together, drinking while he moaned from his sore neck and shoulders.
paragraphs.zh: 他提议：“要不你叫它‘脱壳芝麻’？”她欣然同意，应道：“脱壳芝麻！”于是他们整理好衣服坐在一起喝酒，他则因颈肩酸痛而不停地呻吟。

paragraphs.en: The eldest sister undressed and entered the pool. The porter admired her naked body, comparing it to a full moon or rising sun. He recited:
paragraphs.zh: 大姐脱下衣服，走进了池中。搬运工欣赏着她赤裸的身体，将其比作满月或是初升的太阳，并脱口而出： “她的肌肤如皓月当空，体态宛如旭日东升。”

paragraphs.en: If I compare your figure to the bough, When green, I err and a sore burden bear. The bough is fairest when covered with leaves, And you are fairest when completely bare.
paragraphs.zh: 如果说将你与枝条相比，当枝条青绿时，我犯了错且徒增烦恼。枝条最美丽莫过于繁花似锦，而你则在完全裸露之时最为动人。

paragraphs.en: They continued drinking, enjoying their time together.
paragraphs.zh: 他们继续饮酒，享受着彼此的陪伴。

paragraphs.en: The porter recited verses to a girl by the pool. She rejected each name he proposed with "Bah!" and "Pooh!"
paragraphs.zh: 搬运工对着池边的一个女孩背诵起诗句，每次他提出名字时，她都用“呸！”和“算了吧！”回应。

paragraphs.en: until she slapped him on the neck. Tired of her insults, he finally asked for her suggestion. She suggested the Inn of Abu Masrur.
paragraphs.zh: 直到她一巴掌拍在他的脖子上。受够了她的侮辱，他终于请求她提出建议。她建议他们投宿阿布·马苏尔旅店。

paragraphs.en: He agreed, then they continued drinking.
paragraphs.zh: 他答应了，然后他们继续饮酒。

paragraphs.en: The porter then stripped off his clothes and jumped into the pool.
paragraphs.zh: 然后看门人脱掉衣服跳进了池子里。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, interrupting Shahrazad's story. Dinarzad praised it as delightful. Shahrazad promised a better one the next night if she was spared.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，打断了沙赫拉兹德的故事。迪纳兹德称赞道，这故事真是妙不可言。沙赫拉兹德若能免于今晚的惩罚，保证明晚带来更加精彩的故事。

paragraphs.en: The king vowed to hear more before deciding her fate.
paragraphs.zh: 国王决定在做出判决之前先听听更多的意见。

paragraphs.en: That night, Dinarzad urged Shahrazad to continue her tale. With enthusiasm, Shahrazad agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，丁佐德催促沙赫拉兹德继续讲她的故事。沙赫拉兹德兴致勃勃地答应了。

paragraphs.en: The porter went down to the pool, bathed thoroughly, then rushed out. He planted himself in the lap of the fairest girl, rested his legs in another's lap, and put his arms on yet another's. Pointing to his penis, he asked, "Ladies, what is this?" They found him amusing and laughed.
paragraphs.zh: 搬运工来到池边，洗了个痛快澡后便匆匆跑了出来。他坐到了最漂亮的那位女士的大腿上，另一条腿搭在另一位女士的膝上，双臂则搂着第三位女士。他指着自己的阳具问道：“女士们，这是什么？”她们觉得这很有趣，不禁笑起来。

paragraphs.en: One called it a "cock," but he retorted, "You have no shame; that’s an ugly word." Another said "penis," and he replied, "You should be ashamed; may God put you to shame." A third suggested "dick," which he denied.
paragraphs.zh: 其中一个叫它“公鸡”，但他反驳说：“你没羞没臊的，这词多难听。”另一个说“阴茎”，他回应道：“你应该感到羞耻，愿上帝惩罚你。”第三个提议用“棒子”这个词，但他予以拒绝。

paragraphs.en: When asked about the name, he hugged and kissed them, pinching and biting as they laughed until they fell back. Finally, he admitted it was called the "smashing mule." They inquired further, and he explained that it grazed on basil at bridges, ate husked sesame, and galloped through Abu Masrur's inn.
paragraphs.zh: 当被问及名字时，他一边拥抱亲吻她们，一边笑得前仰后合地掐捏着她们。最终，他承认这个名字叫做“砸锅卖铁的驴子”。她们追问起来，他解释说这头驴子在桥上吃百里香，在磨坊里啃脱壳芝麻，并且穿过阿布·马斯鲁尔的旅店疾驰而过。

paragraphs.en: Laughter ensued once more before they continued their revelry into night.
paragraphs.zh: 他们再次笑过之后，继续狂欢直至深夜。

paragraphs.en: The porter was told by the ladies, "Sir, it's time for you to rise, put on your slippers, and show us your back." He replied, "Where do I go from here? Leaving my body is easier than leaving your company.
paragraphs.zh: 女士们对门房说：“先生，该起床了，穿上拖鞋，让我们看看你的背。”他回答道：“我该怎么办呢？离开你们的陪伴比离开自己的身体还要难。”

paragraphs.en: Let’s join night with day; we can part ways early tomorrow."
paragraphs.zh: 让我们把夜晚算作白天，我们明天早点分手吧。

paragraphs.en: The shopper said, "By God, sisters, he is right. For God's sake, let him stay tonight so we can laugh at him and amuse ourselves. Who will meet such a clever rogue again?
paragraphs.zh: 购物者说道：“天哪，姐妹们，他说得没错。求求你们，让他今晚留下吧，我们可以取笑他一番，消遣一下自己。谁还能再遇到这么机灵的骗子呢？”

paragraphs.en: He is witty and cunning."
paragraphs.zh: 他机智而又狡猾。

paragraphs.en: They insisted, "You cannot spend the night with us unless you agree to our condition: refrain from asking for any explanation of what we do or happens to us. Speak not of what concerns you not, lest you hear what pleases you not." The porter agreed, saying, "Yes, yes, I am dumb and blind."
paragraphs.zh: 他们坚持说道：“如果你不答应我们的条件，就休想在我们这里过夜：不准问我们做什么或发生什么事，不要管那些与你无关的事情，否则你会听到让你不悦的声音。”搬运工应允了，脱口而出：“是的，是的，我什么也不会说，什么也看不见。”

paragraphs.en: They instructed him to rise and go to the entrance, where he found an inscription in gold: "Whoever speaks of what concerns him not hears what pleases him not." He returned and pledged, "I will not speak of what concerns me not."
paragraphs.zh: 他们吩咐他起身，前往门口，在那里他看到用金子刻着的一行字：“谈及他人之事者，听不到令自己愉快之言。”他返回来发誓道：“我不会再谈论他人之事。”

paragraphs.en: After supper, the three ladies lit the lamps and placed aloewood and ambergris into wax to light the candles. The incense filled the hall with its fragrance. They changed the plates, laid out wine and fresh fruits, and sat down to drink and converse.
paragraphs.zh: 晚饭后，三位女士点燃了灯烛，在蜡上放置了沉香和龙涎香来点燃油灯。香烟弥漫着整个大厅的香气。她们换上了新的盘子，摆上了酒和新鲜水果，然后坐下来饮酒聊天。

paragraphs.en: For a long time, they engaged in refined conversation, bantering, laughing, and joking. Suddenly, there was a knock at the door.
paragraphs.zh: 他们长时间地进行着优雅的交谈，互相开玩笑，笑声不断。突然，门上传来敲门声。

paragraphs.en: One of the girls rose to answer it. After a moment, she returned and said, "Sisters, if you listen to me, we will have a delightful night. Three one-eyed dervishes are standing outside.
paragraphs.zh: 其中一个女孩起身去开门。片刻后，她回来说道：“姐妹们，如果你们愿意听我的话，今晚将会非常愉快。门外有三个独眼罗姆人在等着呢。”

paragraphs.en: Each is shaven from head to beard and has only one eye. They just arrived in Baghdad from their travels and need a place to stay for the night."
paragraphs.zh: 每个女人都从头到下巴光秃，只有一只眼睛。她们刚从旅行中回到巴格达，需要找个地方过夜。

paragraphs.en: The ladies were intrigued. "How so?" they asked.
paragraphs.zh: 女士们颇感好奇。“究竟是怎么回事？”她们问道。

paragraphs.en: She replied, "They knocked at our door hoping we would give them the key to the stable or offer them a room. Their faces are peculiar; each would make a mourner laugh. Would you agree to let them in just this once, so that we can amuse ourselves with them tonight and send them on their way early tomorrow?"
paragraphs.zh: 她回答说：“她们敲门，希望我们能给他们打开马厩的钥匙或者让他们住一晚。她们的脸色怪异得很，每个都能让哀悼者开怀一笑。你愿意破例让他们进来一次吗？这样今晚我们可以逗他们玩一阵子，明天早上再把他们送走。”

paragraphs.en: After some persuasion, they agreed but set a condition: "Let them in, but make it clear that they must not speak of what concerns them not, lest they hear something displeasing."
paragraphs.zh: 在一番劝说之后，他们勉强答应了，但设下了一个条件：“放她们进来，不过一定要明确告诉她们，不要谈及无关紧要的事情，以免听到令她们不悦的消息。”

paragraphs.en: The porter, recovering from his beating, sat up and glared at three one-eyed dervishes who entered, followed by three girls. The girls greeted them warmly, expressing delight at their visit and congratulating them on their safe arrival. The dervishes thanked them politely and bowed again.
paragraphs.zh: 被打醒来的搬运工坐起身来，怒视着进来的三个独眼罗宾汉和他们身后的三个姑娘。姑娘们热情地迎接他们，高兴地表示欢迎，并祝贺他们平安抵达。罗宾汉们礼貌地感谢她们，再次鞠躬致意。

paragraphs.en: Upon seeing the beautiful hall, well-set table with wine, nuts, dried fruits, burning candles, and smoking incense, they exclaimed in unison: "By God, this is fine." Turning to the porter, they said, "Whether an Arab or a foreigner, he is a brother dervish."
paragraphs.zh: 见到这座华丽的大厅，桌上摆着美酒、坚果、干果，烛火通明，香烟袅袅，三人不禁异口同声地赞叹：“天哪，这真是太好了。”转向门房，她们说道：“不管他是阿拉伯人还是外国人，他都是我们的兄弟苦行僧。”

paragraphs.en: The porter retorted, "Sit here without meddling. Haven't you read the inscription on the door, which clearly states 'Speak not of what concerns you not, lest you hear what pleases you not'?" The dervishes replied humbly, "O mendicant, we ask for God's forgiveness.
paragraphs.zh: 门丁反驳道：“你们就坐在这里，别多管闲事。你们没看见门口的告示吗？上面明明写着‘勿言己无关之事，以免听闻令你不悦之语’。”乞丐们谦卑地回答说：“施主，请为我们祈祷吧。”

paragraphs.en: Our heads are in your hands." The girls intervened and made peace between them. Then, the shopper offered food to the dervishes, who ate before joining everyone else in carousing and drinking.
paragraphs.zh: “我们的命就掌握在你手里了。”女孩们介入，调解了她们之间的争执。随后，购物者给乞丐施舍食物，乞丐们吃完后也加入了大家的狂欢和饮酒之中。

paragraphs.en: The porter asked, "Friends, can you entertain us with something?"
paragraphs.zh: 搬运工问道：“各位女士，能否给我们表演些什么？”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Her sister Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a lovely and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "What is this compared to the tale I shall tell tomorrow night if I live!"
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫札德默不作声。她的妹妹迪纳兹达说道：“姐姐，这故事多美妙、多有趣啊！”沙赫札德回答道：“比起我明天晚上要讲的故事，这简直不算什么！”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Dinarzad asked her sister Shahrazad, "If you are not sleepy, tell us one of your lovely little tales to while away the night." Shahrazad agreed with pleasure. She recounted how the dervishes, heated by wine, called for musical instruments.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹达对她的妹妹沙赫拉兹达说：“如果你不困，给我们讲一个你那些可爱的小故事吧，打发这漫长的夜晚。”沙赫拉兹达欣然应允。她讲述了那些酒后热血沸腾的苦行僧们呼唤乐器的情景。

paragraphs.en: The doorkeeper brought them a tambourine, flute, and Persian harp. They rose, tuned their instruments, and began to play and sing loudly. While they were performing, they heard knocking at the door, prompting the doorkeeper to investigate.
paragraphs.zh: 门房给他们拿来一面手鼓、一支笛子和一把波斯竖琴。她们站起身来，调好乐器，开始大声地弹奏和歌唱。正当她们表演的时候，门外传来了敲门声，门房只好前去查看。

paragraphs.en: The caliph Harun al-Rashid and Ja’far entered Baghdad one night. Passing by a house, they heard music and laughter. Harun wanted to visit, but Ja’far warned of potential danger.
paragraphs.zh: 哈伦·拉什德苏丹和贾法尔某晚来到了巴格达。他们路过一户人家时，听到里面有音乐和笑声。哈伦想去看看，但贾法尔警告说可能有危险。

paragraphs.en: Despite his concerns, the caliph insisted on entering.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管他心中有所顾虑，哈里发还是坚持要进去。

paragraphs.en: Ja’far knocked at the door. The porter opened it, and Ja’far stepped forward, kissing the ground before her. He explained that they were merchants from Mosul, recently in Baghdad, who had been invited to a party by a local merchant.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔敲了敲门。守门人开了门，贾法尔上前一步，在她面前吻了地面。他解释说他们是从摩苏尔来的商人，最近在巴格达，受一位当地商人的邀请参加了一个聚会。

paragraphs.en: During their celebration, police raided them, causing some injuries and arrests. They sought refuge, fearing further trouble.
paragraphs.zh: 在他们庆祝时，警察突袭了现场，造成了一些伤员并进行了逮捕。他们四处逃散，生怕再惹上麻烦。

paragraphs.en: Ja’far said, "O my lady, we are strangers here. If we continue walking, the prefect might arrest us for intoxication. The inn is locked until morning.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔说：“夫人，我们是外乡人。如果继续走，可能会被那里的官员以醉酒为由抓起来。客栈要到明天才开门。”

paragraphs.en: We heard your music and hope you will let us join in to enjoy the rest of the night. If not, we can sleep in the hallway till sunrise."
paragraphs.zh: 我们听到了你们的音乐，希望你们能让我们也加入，共度今夜余下的时光。如果不方便的话，我们就在走廊里打个地铺，等到天亮再走。

paragraphs.en: The porter relayed their request to the ladies inside.
paragraphs.zh: 门夫将他们的请求转告给了里面三位女士。

paragraphs.en: The doorkeeper, after verifying Ja’far’s speech and their respectable appearance, informed her sisters about them. The girls felt pity and invited them in. Upon entering, the caliph with Ja’far and Masrur greeted everyone, including the porter, who rose to welcome them.
paragraphs.zh: 门卫在核实了贾法尔的言辞和他们端庄的模样后，将这些情况告知了他的姐妹们。女孩们心生怜悯，请她们进屋。一进门，哈里发、贾法尔和马苏尔便向所有人问好，门卫也起身相迎。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad fell silent as morning approached. Dinarzad then said, "What a delightful story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have an even better one."
paragraphs.zh: 随着晨光渐近，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。丁纳兹德then说道：“真是个美妙的故事！”沙赫拉兹德回答道：“等到明天晚上吧；我还有更精彩的一个。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad asked Shahrazad to continue the tale of the three girls. Shahrazad agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，丁拉兹德请沙赫札德继续讲述那三个女孩的故事。沙赫札德答应了。

paragraphs.en: When the caliph and his companions entered, the girls welcomed them with conditions: they must remain silent about what they saw. The caliph accepted, impressed by their beauty and eloquence in a blind dervish community. They conversed and drank, with the dervishes playing music between rounds.
paragraphs.zh: 当哈里发和他的同伴进入时，那三位女士提出了一个条件：他们必须对所见之事保持沉默。哈里发欣然接受了这一要求，被她们在盲人苦行僧群体中的美丽与 eloquence 所打动。大家交谈甚欢，还边喝边聊，期间苦行僧们在一旁奏起了音乐。

paragraphs.en: When the wine had taken effect, the mistress of the house rose and took the shopper by the hand, saying, "Sister, let us do our duty." The sisters agreed. The doorkeeper cleared the table, removed the peels and shells, replenished the incense, and arranged the dervishes on a sofa at one side of the hall.
paragraphs.zh: 酒力发作后，女主人起身拉着购物者的手说：“姐妹们，让我们尽到责任吧。”姐妹俩应允了。门房清理了桌子，收走了果皮和壳子，又添上了香料，并在大厅一侧的沙发上安排了几位圣徒。

paragraphs.en: She then seated Ja’far and Masrur on another sofa opposite.
paragraphs.zh: 她随后让贾法尔和马斯鲁尔坐在对面的另一张沙发上。

paragraphs.en: "Get up and lend us a hand," she commanded the porter. The porter got up, girded himself, and asked, "What is it?" She replied, "Stand where you are."
paragraphs.zh: “快起来，帮我们一把。”她对搬运工下令。搬运工起身整理了一下衣服，问道：“出了什么事？”她回答说：“就站在那儿别动。”

paragraphs.en: Placing a chair in the middle of the hall, the shopper opened a cupboard and said to the porter, "Come and help me."
paragraphs.zh: 在大厅中央放了一把椅子，购物者打开一个柜子，对门丁说：“过来帮我一下。”

paragraphs.en: The porter approached and saw two black female hounds with chains around their necks. He took them and led them to the center of the hall. The mistress of the house came forward, rolled up her sleeves, and took a braided whip.
paragraphs.zh: 门房走近，看到有两个戴着颈圈的黑犬。他把它们抓起来，带到大厅中央。女主人走了出来，卷起袖子，拿起一根编织的鞭子。

paragraphs.en: She called to the porter, "Bring me one of the bitches."
paragraphs.zh: 她对着门房喊道：“给我拿一只母狗过来。”

paragraphs.en: The porter dragged one of the bitches by the chain, while she wept and shook her head at the girl. As the porter held the chain, the girl struck the bitch with hard blows on the sides, causing it to howl and weep. She continued until her arm grew weary.
paragraphs.zh: 搬运工拽着一条狗的链子，那条狗一边呜咽着，一边对着女孩摇头。搬运工握着链子的时候，女孩用力拍打那条狗的侧身，让它哀嚎不已。她一直这样打下去，直到手臂感到酸痛。

paragraphs.en: Stopping, she threw the whip away, took the chain from the porter, embraced the bitch, and began to cry. The bitch also cried, and they wept together for a long time. The girl wiped the bitch’s tears with her handkerchief, kissed her on the head, and said to the porter, "Take her back to her place, and bring me the other."
paragraphs.zh: 停了下来，她扔掉了鞭子，从搬运工手中接过链子，拥抱了那只母狗，开始哭泣。母狗也跟着哭了起来，她们一起哭了好一会儿。女孩用她的手帕擦干了母狗的眼泪，在它头上吻了一下，对搬运工说道：“你把它送回原来的地方去，再把另外那一只带给我。”

paragraphs.en: The porter took the first bitch to the cupboard, brought the second one to the girl, who treated it as she had the first. She beat it until it fainted. Then she took the bitch, cried with her, kissed her on the head, and asked the porter to take her back to her sister.
paragraphs.zh: 搬运工把第一条狗带到柜子里，然后带第二条狗给那个女孩。女孩对待第二条狗就像第一条一样，打得它晕了过去。随后她抱着这条狗哭了起来，亲吻着它的头，并请搬运工把她送回姐姐那里。

paragraphs.en: Those present were amazed by what they saw. The caliph himself was troubled, burning with curiosity about the story of these two bitches. He winked at Ja’far, but Ja’far signaled him not to inquire further.
paragraphs.zh: 在场的人都被眼前的情景惊呆了。哈里发自己也显得有些不安，对这两名女子的故事充满了好奇。他朝贾法尔眨了眨眼，但贾法尔示意他不要再多问。

paragraphs.en: The doorkeeper sat and said to the shopper, "Get up and pay your debt." The shopper rose, entered a chamber, returned with a bag of yellow satin adorned with green silk tassels and ambergris beads. She seated herself before him, drew out a lute, placed it on her knee, and began to play and sing:
paragraphs.zh: 门房坐下来对顾客说：“快起来还债。”顾客起身，走进一间房间，回来时手里拿着一个饰有绿丝穗和琥珀珠的黄色丝绸袋子。她坐在门房对面，拿出一把琵琶放在膝上，开始弹奏并歌唱：

paragraphs.en: "My love, you are my aim, And you are my desire. Your company is constant joy, Your absence, hellish fire. You are the madness of my life, My one infatuation, A love in which there is no shame, A blameless adoration."
paragraphs.zh: 我的爱，你是我的追求，你是我的渴望。你的陪伴是我永恒的快乐，你的缺席则是无尽的煎熬。你是我生命的疯狂，我唯一的迷恋，一种毫无愧疚的爱情，一份纯洁的倾慕。

paragraphs.en: Her tears declared her passion as they flowed down her cheeks. The doorkeeper listened to her song, his expression unreadable.
paragraphs.zh: 她的泪水在脸颊上滑落，宣泄着她的情感。门卫听着她的歌声，脸上表情毫无波动。

paragraphs.en: Morning came and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad asked, "Sister, what an amazing story!" Shahrazad replied, "Tomorrow night, I will tell you one even more delightful."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙海拉罕默然不语。丁佐拉德问道：“姐姐，真是个精彩的故事！”沙海拉罕回答道：“明天晚上，我还会给你讲一个更加动听的。”

paragraphs.en: The next evening, Dinarzad urged Shahrazad, "Tell us a tale to pass the time." Shahrazad agreed and began her narrative.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，丁拉兹达催促沙赫札德说：“给我们讲个故事打发时间吧。”沙赫札德答应了，并开始了她的讲述。

paragraphs.en: The girl recited a poem about unending love. Her sister cried out and tore her dress, fainting on the ground. The caliph saw whip marks on her body and was troubled.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩朗诵了一首关于永恒之爱的诗。她的妹妹突然喊叫起来，扯坏了衣服，昏倒在了地上。哈里发看到她身上有鞭痕，显得颇为不安。

paragraphs.en: He asked Ja’far for an explanation.
paragraphs.zh: 他向贾法尔求个明白。

paragraphs.en: Ja’far advised against it, citing their agreement not to discuss matters unrelated to them.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔劝阻他们，引述了他们之前不讨论无关事务的约定。

paragraphs.en: The shopper entered with a new dress for the sister, replacing the torn one. She then served more drink and played a lute, singing:
paragraphs.zh: 购物者进来为姐姐带来了新裙子，换下了破旧的那一件。随后她又端上了酒水，并弹起竖琴唱起了歌：

paragraphs.en: If I miss you, what will you say? If I long for you, how can I convey my pain? Sending someone won't help, For love's loss is unbearable.
paragraphs.zh: 如果我思念你，你会怎么说？若我对你的思念化作痛苦，又该如何向你倾诉？派人传达也无济于事，因为失恋的痛苦难以言表。

paragraphs.en: Only longing remains, Tears falling down my face. You who taught me to love, Stay in my heart forever.
paragraphs.zh: 只剩下思念，泪水滑落脸庞。你曾教会我爱，永远驻留在我心间。

paragraphs.en: When the sister finished her song, the girl cried out, "Oh, oh, oh!" and tore her dress. She fainted, and upon waking, the shopper dressed her in a better gown.
paragraphs.zh: 当姐姐唱完歌，女孩惊呼一声“哦，哦，哦！”扯破了衣服，晕了过去。醒来后，购物者给她换上了一件更好的裙子。

paragraphs.en: The sister then pleaded for payment, saying they had only one more song left.
paragraphs.zh: 随后姐姐恳求道，她们只剩下最后一首歌了，请先付酬。

paragraphs.en: The shopper replied with pleasure and began to play and sing:
paragraphs.zh: 购物者愉快地回答道，并开始边玩边唱：

paragraphs.en: How long shall I endure this cruel disdain? Have I not paid enough with tears of woe?
paragraphs.zh: 我还要忍受这种残酷的冷落多久？我已经用无尽的哀伤之泪付出了足够的代价吗？

paragraphs.en: For how long suffer your willful neglect, As if it were a vengeful, envious foe?
paragraphs.zh: 你为何如此任性忽视，仿佛那是报复心强的敌人？

paragraphs.en: Be kind! Your cruel ways inflict a cruel pain, Master, 'tis time to me you pity show.
paragraphs.zh: 慈悲为怀！您残忍的举止带来了深深的痛苦，请对我施以怜悯。

paragraphs.en: O gentlemen, avenge this thrall of love, Who neither sleep nor patience does now know.
paragraphs.zh: 贤士们，请为这份爱情的囚徒讨回公道， 她已无眠无耐，再无分毫忍耐之心。

paragraphs.en: Morning came and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad praised her sister's story, saying it was amazing and entertaining. Shahrazad promised to tell an even stranger tale the next night if she survived.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默然不语。丁纳扎德称赞姐姐的故事精彩绝伦、引人入胜。沙赫拉兹德承诺如果自己能熬过今晚，明天晚上将讲述一个更加离奇的故事。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Dinarzad urged Shahrazad to continue the story of the girls.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹达催促沙赫拉扎德继续讲述那三个女孩的故事。

paragraphs.en: The girl exclaimed after hearing the third song, "By God, this is good." She tore her dress and fainted, revealing whip marks on her chest. The dervishes muttered their displeasure, wishing they had stayed outside the city instead.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩听完第三首歌后脱口而出：“天哪，真好。”她扯破了衣服晕了过去，胸部露出鞭痕。苦行僧们低声抱怨着，后悔没有留在城外。

paragraphs.en: The caliph asked them why they were upset. They replied that their minds were troubled by what they saw. He then inquired about the two black women and the girl.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发问她们为何心绪不宁，她们回答说，所见之事令她们颇感困扰。接着，他询问起那两个黑妇人和女孩的情况。

paragraphs.en: The dervishes admitted they knew nothing until tonight. Surprised, the caliph turned to the porter, who denied knowing anything, saying he had never entered this house before today.
paragraphs.zh: 乞丐们直到今晚才知道什么都不知道。哈里发闻言惊讶地转向搬运工，而搬运工否认知道任何事情，并声称自己在此之前从未踏入过这座房子。

paragraphs.en: The caliph proposed a plan: with Ja’far and Masrur included, there were seven men and only three women. They decided to ask for an explanation, threatening force if necessary. However, Ja’far objected, reminding them they were guests and should keep silent as the night was almost over.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发提出一个计划：包括贾法尔和马苏尔在内，共有七名男子和三名女子。他们决定要求解释，必要时威胁使用武力。然而，贾法尔提出了异议，提醒大家他们是客人，应该保持沉默，因为夜幕即将降临。

paragraphs.en: Ja’far whispered to the caliph that he would return in the morning with the women's story. But the caliph insisted on questioning them immediately. Ja’far argued against this, but they eventually agreed that the porter should ask first.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔小声对哈里发说他会第二天早上回来讲述那三位女士的故事，但哈里发坚持要立即对他们进行质询。贾法尔据理力争，但最终大家同意由搬运工先开口。

paragraphs.en: The porter was then tasked with leading the conversation, setting the stage for what was to come.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，看门人被委托主导对话，为接下来的故事做铺垫。

paragraphs.en: The girls heard the men's clamor. One asked, "Men, what do you want?" The porter approached and said, "My lady, these men wish to hear the story of the two black bitches and why they are punished, as well as your sister’s tale."
paragraphs.zh: 女孩们听到了男人们的喧哗。其中一个问道：“先生们，你们想要什么？”门丁走近说道：“夫人，这些先生想听听那两个黑贱妇的故事以及她们为何受罚，还有您妹妹的故事。”

paragraphs.en: Turning to them, a girl asked, "Is this true?" They all agreed except Ja’far. She then said, "O guests, you have wronged us.
paragraphs.zh: 转向那三位女士，一个女孩问道：“这是真的吗？”除了贾法尔之外，她们都一致表示赞同。接着她说：“各位客官，你们冤枉我们了。”

paragraphs.en: We took you in and fed you, but you meddled and did us harm."
paragraphs.zh: 我们收留了你，还给你吃了饭，可你却没事找事，给我们惹了麻烦。

paragraphs.en: Rolling up her sleeves, she struck the floor three times, calling for seven black men with drawn swords. Each man struck one of the guests, binding them and leading them to the hall center. The black men stood above their captives with drawn swords.
paragraphs.zh: 卷起袖子，她连敲三下地面，呼唤来七名手持利剑的黑衣壮汉。每名壮汉上前击倒一位宾客，将他们捆绑起来，押到了大厅中央。那几名黑衣壮汉则站在宾客上方，手中紧握着剑。

paragraphs.en: "O most honorable lady," said the porter, "do not punish me for another's sin. All these men sinned except me. By God, we had a delightful day if only we could escape these one-eyed dervishes."
paragraphs.zh: “最尊贵的女士，”搬运工说道，“请不要因为我人的过错而惩罚我。除了我之外，这些人都犯了错。天哪，如果我们能避开这些独眼苦行僧，我们的日子该有多愉快啊。”

paragraphs.en: He began to weep and recited:
paragraphs.zh: 他开始哭泣，并念诵道：

paragraphs.en: Fair is the forgiveness of mighty men, And fairest when to weakest men 'tis shown. Break off not the first friendship for the last, By the bond of love that has between us grown.
paragraphs.zh: 宽恕伟大之人是美好的，而对弱者展现的宽恕最为美好。不要因为最后的友谊就中断了最初的情谊，那是爱的纽带在我们之间逐渐形成的。

paragraphs.en: The girl, despite her anger, laughed and approached the group. "Tell me who you are," she said, "for you have only an hour to live. If you were not of noble birth or powerful rulers, you would not dare offend us."
paragraphs.zh: 女孩虽然怒气未消，还是笑了起来，走近众人。“告诉我你们是谁吧，”她说，“因为你们只剩下一个小时的命了。如果你们不是出身高贵或权势显赫之人，是不敢冒犯我们的。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph ordered Ja’far, "Tell her who we are; otherwise, we might be killed by mistake."
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发命令贾法尔：“告诉她我们是谁；否则，我们可能会被误杀。”

paragraphs.en: Ja’far replied, "This is part of our punishment." The caliph snapped, "Not now, man. Tell the truth!"
paragraphs.zh: Ja’far 回答说：“这是我们受罚的一部分。”哈里发不耐烦地说道，“不是现在，伙计。说实话！”

paragraphs.en: The lady then asked the dervishes if they were brothers. They denied it and explained their individual stories. Each claimed to have lost an eye in a strange accident that led them to become dervishes.
paragraphs.zh: 女士接着问这些苦行僧是否是兄弟。他们否认了这一说法，并各自讲述了他们的故事。每个人都说自己是在一场奇怪的事故中失明，从而成为了苦行僧。

paragraphs.en: They each came from different cities and were sons of kings or princes.
paragraphs.zh: 她们分别来自不同的城市，有的是国王的儿子，有的是王子。

paragraphs.en: The girl told the black men, "If any of you tell your tales, I will let you go. But if not, prepare for death."
paragraphs.zh: 女孩对那几个黑人说道：“如果你们当中谁都不讲自己的故事，我就让你们活命。但如果有人开口，那就做好死亡的准备吧。”

paragraphs.en: Morning arrived, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said to her sister, "What an amazing story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; this is nothing compared to what I'll tell then."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。丁纳札德对她说：“真是个奇妙的故事！”沙赫拉兹德回答道：“等到明天晚上再听吧；那可比今晚的精彩多了。”

paragraphs.en: The porter recounted his journey from the vintner to the fruit vendor and finally to this house, saying he would not leave until he heard the tales of others. The girl dismissed him with a simple command: "Stroke your head and go."
paragraphs.zh: 搬运工讲述了从酒商到水果贩再到这家宅邸的旅程，表示自己绝不会离开，直到听闻其他人的故事。女孩只简单地命令了一句：“摸摸你的头，走吧。”

paragraphs.en: Then, the first dervish stepped forward. Baghdad, once the capital of the Abbasid caliphate, was situated on the Tigris River. It is where several stories from the Arabian Nights are set.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，第一个苦行僧上前一步。巴格达曾是阿拔斯王朝的首都，坐落在底格里斯河畔。那里也是《一千零一夜》中多个故事的发生地。

paragraphs.en: The first dervish began his tale, speaking of a black eunuch who served as Harun al-Rashid's executioner and bodyguard. Harun al-Rashid, the fifth Abbasid caliph, ruled during the golden age of the Arab empire. His vizier, Ja’far al-Barmaki, was frequently at his side until he was executed for suspected treachery.
paragraphs.zh: 第一个苦行僧开始了他的讲述，说起一个黑奴宦官如何在哈伦·拉希德的宫廷中担任刽子手和贴身护卫。哈伦·拉希德是第五任阿拔斯王朝哈里发，在阿拉伯帝国黄金时代的统治时期长达数十年之久。他的首相贾法尔·巴尔马基经常伴其左右，直到因涉嫌叛逆被处决。

paragraphs.en: The dervish recited a verse form in quatrains that originated in Baghdad, often starting with "kan," meaning "once upon a time."
paragraphs.zh: 乞丐吟诵了一首起源于巴格达、以“kan”（从前）开头的四行诗。
